AUTHOR: Marrable
TITLE: Accelerating Species Recognition and Labelling of Fish From Underwater Video With Machine-Assisted Deep Learning
REGION: Australia (OzFish BRUVS from AIMS/UWA/Curtin; out-of-sample RUV datasets from Queensland)
SPECIES: 12 most abundant OzFish species (incl. Lethrinus punctulatus, Lutjanus sebae) + catch-all 'fish' class; fish-only detector
DATA: OzFish subset relabelled with boxes (1,751 images, 42,685 objects); out-of-sample: DeepFish (1,600 localisation images), Dataset A (Lopez-Marcano 2021b), Dataset B (Ditria 2021), Dataset C (Lopez 2021)
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'the model identifying fish against backgrounds of a range of habitat types (such as seagrass, sand, and coral) and in a range of water conditions and clarities'
D_EV: Sec. 2.3: 'The box-and-labelled data were split into train, validation, and test sets with 66%, 17%, and 17% by class, respectively.'
R_EV: Table 2: OzFish (not out-of-sample) recall 0.699 vs out-of-sample Dataset A 0.701, B 0.885, C 0.786, DeepFish 0.700; Sec 2.3: 'four completely independently collected and published, out-of-sample datasets'
C_EV: Sec. 2.4.2: 'All models were given a confidence threshold of 0.5, meaning any predictions with a confidence less than 0.5 were ignored.'
E_EV: Table 3: 'Summary of the datasets used for evaluating the species classification performance on the OzFish test data.' Only precision/recall/F1 and label proportions reported.
METR: Precision, recall, F1; recall only for out-of-sample sets; proportion auto-labelled
NOTE: D: own 66/17/17 split of OzFish subset 'by class'; unit (image vs object) and whether video-grouped not stated -> coded image random (lower information). R: external test on four independent RUV datasets (different platform, habitats, species), recall only (no precision possible); numeric comparison to in-domain recall available -> R3 Y. C: default 0.5 threshold used as-is with no sweep, but false positives discussed extensively; C_ALL rules have a gap here - coded N (lower information); verifier check. C4 = Y because a catch-all 'fish' class is used to absorb species outside the 12 targets (open-set handling) - debatable, it is a trained 'other' class rather than a reject option. E4 FNR because text states ~30% of fish missed. Code: Jupyter notebook for data prep on GitHub (training code is standard YOLOv5). Habitats include seagrass, sand, coral.
